item.title: U.S. Forest Service to keep some research stations open, after pushback about restructuring
item.description: In a massive restructuring under the Trump administration, U.S. Forest Service is closing dozens of research stations but, as NPR's Chiara Eisner reports, it is keeping some facilities open that had been projected to shutter.
item.content:encoded: In a massive restructuring under the Trump administration, U.S. Forest Service is closing dozens of research stations but, as NPR's Chiara Eisner reports, it is keeping some facilities open that had been projected to shutter.
item.dc:creator: Chiara Eisner

item.title: I don't think I had $10 in the bank: Angela Davis remembers Gloria Steinem's allyship
item.description: Activist and author Angela Davis remembers her friend Gloria Steinem, and discusses intersectional feminism today.
item.content:encoded: Activist and author Angela Davis remembers her friend Gloria Steinem, and discusses intersectional feminism today.

item.title: Jazz legend John Coltrane's Philadelphia house to become a cultural heritage site
item.description: On the centennial of father's birth, Ravi Coltrane talks about turning the home where the jazz legend spent a crucial period in the 1950s into a cultural heritage and community space.
item.content:encoded: On the centennial of father's birth, Ravi Coltrane talks about turning the home where the jazz legend spent a crucial period in the 1950s into a cultural heritage and community space.

item.title: The Republican midterm convention is taking place in the heart of Bush country
item.description: The Republican midterm convention in Dallas takes place in the same city that helped give rise to the Bush political dynasty. Still, many policies championed by the conservative presidents are noticeably absent from today's Republican Party.
item.content:encoded: The Republican midterm convention in Dallas takes place in the same city that helped give rise to the Bush political dynasty. Still, many policies championed by the conservative presidents are noticeably absent from today's Republican Party.

item.title: Covering the wild world of prediction markets
item.description: NPR's Bobby Allyn talks about covering the prediction markets, where anyone can trade bets on the outcome of anything happening in the real world.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy trial deadlock leaves law and maternal health at a crossroads
item.description: The Lindsay Clancy trial ended in mistrial. The case has led to greater public awareness and discussion about maternal mental health, specifically postpartum psychosis.
item.content:encoded: The Lindsay Clancy trial ended in mistrial. The case has led to greater public awareness and discussion about maternal mental health, specifically postpartum psychosis.

item.title: On the Line: Wildland firefighter Justin Brown on battling a historic fire season
item.description: The wildfire season in the western U.S. is one of the worst on record. NPR's Scott Simon talks to Justin Brown, a wildland firefighter, about the challenges in tackling today's blazes.

item.title: Voters are fed up with data centers. Both parties are trying to cash in for midterms
item.description: Democrats and Republicans have found common ground in this campaign season. Both parties have poured millions into ads attacking data centers as the public continues to protest the AI facilities.
